summary: Six sampled forms share one cloud of splats. The Lorenz equations, figure-eight Klein-bottle parametrization, gyroid approximation, and QR encoder have reference sources. The word and loop are graphic designs; flights, pushes, colors, and the two-ink treatment are animation choices.

claims.claim: The word form samples the site's five-by-seven bitmap glyphs.
claims.how: Set bits in the existing glyph table become filled cells sampled by splats. Text is uppercased, limited to 24 characters, and wrapped after eight characters per line; unsupported characters become question marks.

sources.title: Splashery's bitmap font
sources.says: The font defines seven rows of five bits per glyph and exports them as the BITMAP table.

claims.note: The test checks finite, deterministic builds; the glyph design comes from the published source table. This is stylized bitmap lettering.

claims.claim: The Lorenz form uses dx/dt = 10(y - x), dy/dt = x(28 - z) - y, and dz/dt = xy - (8/3)z.
claims.how: The derivative uses sigma = 10, rho = 28, and beta = 8/3. A fixed-step RK4 path uses step 0.007, discards 800 warm-up steps, and stores 18,000 points before display sampling, axis reordering, centering, and scaling.

sources.title: Lorenz attractor
sources.says: The Lorenz equations are X' = sigma(Y - X), Y' = -XZ + rX - Y, and Z' = XY - bZ.

sources.title: Lorenz system
sources.says: The commonly illustrated attractor uses rho = 28, sigma = 10, and beta = 8/3.

claims.note: The test checks two independent derivative values and all three equilibria. This is a finite numerical trajectory, not weather data or a forecast.

claims.claim: The Klein form depicts a figure-eight Klein bottle with the expected self-intersections of a three-dimensional view.
claims.how: The existing Splat equation preset at time zero evaluates R = 2 + cos(u/2)sin(v) - sin(u/2)sin(2v), x = R cos(u), y = sin(u/2)sin(v) + cos(u/2)sin(2v), and z = R sin(u), for u and v from 0 to 2pi. The published figure-eight formula's y and z axes are exchanged; a display rotation and uniform fit follow.

sources.title: Klein bottle
sources.says: The figure-eight parametrization rotates and twists a figure eight, with radial factor a + cos(u/2)sin(v) - sin(u/2)sin(2v). A three-dimensional Klein-bottle picture is an immersion, rather than a self-intersection-free embedding.

claims.note: The reference states a > 2; the existing preset chooses radius parameter 2 for its graphic depiction. Tests check four reference points, not a proof of regularity or topology.

claims.claim: The gyroid form samples the trigonometric approximation sin(x)cos(y) + sin(y)cos(z) + sin(z)cos(x) = 0.
claims.how: Projected samples are accepted only when the implicit-field residual is at most 0.0001, then clipped to a ball of radius 2pi and fitted for display. The test undoes the display fit and checks sampled Float32 residuals within 0.00011.

sources.title: Gyroid
sources.says: The gyroid minimal surface can be trigonometrically approximated by sin(x)cos(y) + sin(y)cos(z) + sin(z)cos(x) = 0.

sources.title: Gyroid
sources.says: The gyroid is an infinitely connected periodic minimal surface discovered by Schoen in 1970.

claims.note: A small residual verifies the chosen trigonometric field, not exact minimal curvature. The display is a finite patch, not the infinite mathematical surface.

claims.claim: The loop form is a decorative, flat three-node diagram, not a simulated orbit or a computed attractor.
claims.how: The sampler places a filled disk, two rings, straight connectors, and an upper arc at fixed two-dimensional coordinates. Splats move between this drawing and the other forms only through the shared animation.

sources.title: Shape morph's loop sampler
sources.says: The loop sampler draws disks, rings, connectors, and an arc with z fixed to zero; it does not integrate a dynamical system.

claims.note: Its geometry and colors are graphic choices with no physical interpretation.

claims.claim: The QR form uses the vendored QR Code Model 2 encoder at error-correction level M and includes a four-module quiet zone.
claims.how: Selecting QR imports the shared encoder, calls it with level M and boosting disabled, and samples its dark and light modules with four blank modules on every side. The editable input accepts up to 42 UTF-8 bytes; a browser test submits 21 accented letters, exactly 42 bytes, and checks the resulting encoded text and level.

sources.title: QR Code generator library
sources.says: The library generates raw QR Code Model 2 modules, supports all four error-correction levels, and allows the caller to disable error-correction boosting.

sources.title: Point for determining the code area
sources.says: A QR Code requires a clear four-module margin on all sides.

claims.note: The 42-byte limit is a display-budget choice, not the QR standard's capacity limit. The form's render tests also decode shorter messages; readability during a flight or from an oblique view is not guaranteed.

simplified: Every form is a finite splat sample, centered and scaled for the same camera; the splats are not a surface mesh.
The Lorenz trajectory is sampled from one fixed-step numerical path. Flights between forms and the spring-back push are animation choices, not Lorenz dynamics or material physics.
The Klein bottle is shown with self-intersections in three dimensions. Its radius, orientation, and colored bands are display choices.
The gyroid uses a trigonometric approximation to the minimal surface and clips it to a finite ball.
The word and loop are graphic designs. The two-ink treatment changes colors, without simulating ink or printing.
